title: Intermittent brownout reset on relay actuation
symptom: The controller restarted every time the relay coil was de-energized. A 15 ms software debounce on the drive pin did not change the behaviour.

measurements.label: 3.3 V rail minimum at coil dropout
3.3 V rail steady state after the fix

rootCause: The coil was switched without suppression, so its inductive kickback reached the shared 3.3 V rail and pulled it below the controller’s brownout threshold.
fix: A 1N4007 diode was fitted antiparallel across the coil terminals.
verification: The rail held 3.28 V across fifty consecutive actuations with no reset, and a second capture at the same probe position showed no sag.

rulesLearned.title: Clamp an inductive load before the first actuation test
rulesLearned.body: A coil switched from a logic rail needs its flyback diode fitted before power is applied, not after a reset is observed.

rulesLearned.title: A timing change cannot fix an electrical transient
rulesLearned.body: Debounce addresses contact bounce on the input side; it does nothing about back-EMF on the output side.

mediaCaption: Flyback diode across the relay coil
